title: Doing life together Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’My command is this: Love each other as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends. You are my friends if you do what I command. I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master’s business. Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you. You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you so that you might go and bear fruit—fruit that will last—and so that whatever you ask in my name the Father will give you. This is my command: Love each other.’’
devotional:
Being a friend means that we understand the dynamics and the expectations of the friendship.

Often when it comes to friendships we are reluctant to express any expectations or aspirations we may have. Jesus did not suffer from this kind of reluctance, he said, ‘You are my friends if you do what I command you.’ John 15:14. This is not to suggest that we are to command our friends to do certain things. But it is suggesting that we should have appropriate and realistic expectations of the friendship.

When it comes to friendship there are two kinds of expectations that are equally wrong. There is a too high expectation which usually kills the friendship by making us demanding, controlling and selfish. The other is having too low or no expectations at all. These kinds of friendships are usually put onto ‘automatic pilot,’ and before you know it friendships are reduced to acquaintances. With no expectations’ comes no commitment.

Being a friend requires open vulnerability.

Look at what Jesus said: -‘’I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master’s business. Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you.’ John 15:15.

This has massive implications. For Jesus there was a connection between being open and learning from his Father, and being open with others. In the mind and experience of Jesus these two things are connected, they are linked, they are indissoluble. The heart attitudes that we require so we can open ourselves up to God in order to hear what he wants to say to us, are the same heart attitudes required to open ourselves up to others. Both these things require vulnerability.

The things that we learn from the Father will always encourage and enhance our friendships. As we listen to God our capacity to enter into meaningful, God pleasing friendships will increase.

Friendships need time to develop. Jesus says a very interesting thing to his disciples. ‘I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master’s business. Instead, I have called you friends.’ Through time, Jesus’ relationship with His disciples changed, it grew, it matured, the dynamics of the friendship changed. This is not an automatic certainty; growth in friendship must be intentional. Growth in friendships will change how we view the other person. Our understanding and perception of the other person will gradually change.

Authentic friendship could be understood as a reflection of election. What do I mean? In verse 16 Jesus said, ‘You have not chosen me but I have chosen you,’ Bible teachers, rightly use this as one of the verses to teach about election. According to one Greek scholar one of the meanings of the word for chosen, eklegomai in classical literature carries the idea of selecting something that is beautiful or praise worthy. It was also used to describe the appointment of soldiers and judges. This is very important. God will never choose us because we are beautiful or praise worthy people. He will never choose us because we are strong soldiers and wise judges. But, he does choose us for the potential he sees in us; he knows that his grace can transform us. Remember the first words Jesus spoke to Peter, ‘You are... you will be...’ John 1:42.

What has that all to do with friendship?

Because we are created in the image of God, there should be something built into all of us that chooses to befriend others, not because they are beautiful people, but because we see potential in them that no one else may see. We should become intentional in our friendships; we should befriend those who are weak, those who are in need, because we understand the potential of the grace of God.

Unfortunately if we’re being honest, we choose to spend time with like minded people, with those who don’t require a huge amount of our energy a lot of the time, and yes at times this is okay. But we need to see in the text, that the disciples who were difficult and at times slow to understand Jesus, were chosen by Him and the relationship changed from discipleship to friendship.
prayer: Father may my friendship with others help them discover their potential.
